Evidence:
[1] Thomas Horn, Jr. (November 21, 1860 – November 20, 1903) was an American Old West scout, who carried out varied roles as hired gunman, Pinkerton, range detective, cowboy, and soldier.
[2] Believed to have committed 17 killings as a hired gunman in the West, in 1902 Horn was convicted of the murder of 14-year-old Willie Nickell near Iron Mountain, Wyoming.
[3] William Brydges was a Canadian man whose arrest for murder resulted in the leading Supreme Court of Canada case "R v Brydges" on the right of a detainee to access duty counsel.
[4] He is best known for the arrest of gunman Tom Horn in 1903 for the alleged murder of 14‑year-old sheepherder Willie Nickell, which has since come into question, and it has long been believed that Lefors falsified evidence helping to convict the wrong man for the murder.

Notes:
[verification] Willie Nickell was the son of Kels Nickell, a sheep rancher in Wyoming.
